analysis.title: Strong US economic data keep gold under pressure
key_insights: Stronger US labor market data and above-consensus inflation lifted yields, supported the USD and weighed on gold. Gold's gains after the US midterm elections were short-lived.
Fed official Waller's comments about discussing a 50bps rate hike at the December meeting added to the repricing of Fed rate expectations toward further hikes.
Gold ETF holdings stayed relatively resilient, while net positioning adjustments were more pronounced in gold futures markets.
UBS says gold could face ongoing headwinds into 1Q27, with meaningful technical support only at around USD 3,500/oz. It does not expect the recent decline to persist throughout 2027.

The drivers of last year's rally into 1Q26 (expected Fed cuts, tariff concerns, Fed independence questions, a perceived preference for a weaker USD) have weakened. Inflation has shifted rate expectations toward hikes, and Fed independence concerns have eased as the Fed raised rates without material intervention from the administration. The AI investment boom has supported US activity. These could be read as driving a full retracement of the rally toward USD 3,500/oz.

UBS argues the market is overly optimistic about US economic resilience and may overestimate both the level and duration of higher rates. It expects inflation to level off and US activity to moderate slightly in 2027, moving rate expectations from further hikes to a pause, then cuts later in the year.
UBS expects central banks, particularly the Fed, to move from hikes to a pause, followed by renewed expectations of cuts, which should support a recovery in gold demand and prices.

Near-term, above-potential US growth, persistent inflation and a hawkish Fed that keep real yields elevated are likely to outweigh longer-term supports such as the US fiscal deficit trajectory and structural USD headwinds.

Watch items: softer US activity in 1Q on higher rates and compressed real wage growth, broader disinflation from 2Q as base effects take hold, and a possible equity pullback as a risk scenario (not the base case) that would support gold. An AI-narrative setback would lower growth and rate-hike expectations and weaken the USD.
UBS expects continued central bank reserve-diversification demand and a jewelry demand recovery at lower prices. It expects these to stabilize gold rather than drive prices higher.

Gold's price relative to other assets is near longer-term averages, its peak-to-trough decline appears advanced by historical standards, and the metal is technically oversold. UBS cautions against extrapolating the downtrend.

UBS sees an attractive risk-reward for a long gold position, given the year-end 2027 target of USD 5,000/oz, the forward curve near USD 3,900/oz and volatility of about 25%. It also reiterates that selling volatility is an attractive way to benefit indirectly, provided the seller can take a long gold position if prices fall much further.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Hawkish repricing strengthened the USD and pressured gold. UBS expects a shift to a pause and then renewed cut expectations in 2027.
Shifted rate expectations toward hikes. UBS expects inflation to level off and broader disinflation from 2Q27 as base effects take hold.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects inflation to level off, US activity to moderate in 2027 and rate expectations to move from hikes to a pause and then cuts. Gold is technically oversold, the decline is advanced by historical standards, and central bank and jewelry demand should help stabilize it.
tension_points.bear_case: Above-potential US growth, persistent inflation and a hawkish Fed keep real yields elevated. The fading of last year's rally drivers could lead to a full retracement toward USD 3,500/oz.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gold falling through technical support near USD 3,500/oz, or a sustained run of hot US inflation and growth data that keeps real yields elevated into 1Q27.
